'''''Agave mitis''''' is a plant species native to the Mexican states of [[Hidalgo (state)|Hidalgo]], [[Tamaulipas]] and [[San Luis Potosí]],<ref>[http://www.rarepalmseeds.com/es/pix/AgaMit.shtml Rare Palm Seeds]</ref> referred to as ''Agave celsii'' in many publications.<ref name=WCSP/><ref>Eggli, U. (ed.) (2001). Illustrated Handbook of Succulent Plants: Monocotyledons: 1-354. Springer-Verlag, Berlin, Heidelberg, New York.</ref>

''Agave mitis'' forms [[rosette (botany)|rosettes]] of blue-green to yellow-green, fleshy leaves up to 60 cm (2 feet) long. The leaves have soft brown spines not nearly as imposing as those of other agaves.<ref>Gentry, H. S. 1982. Agaves of Continental North America. Tucson.</ref><ref>[http://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=3086 San Marcos Growers]</ref> The flowering stalk is up to 2.5 m (8 feet) tall, with the flowers closely appressed against the stem forming a narrow column much more compact than most other species of the genus. Flowers are green, each up to 60 mm (2.4 inches) long.<ref>[http://fhnavajoirt.org/Agave%20mitis.htm Yuccagarten Mannheim Botanischer Garten, Agavaceae Nolinaceae Cactaceae, Mannheim, Germany]</ref>

Because the species is widespread and grows in several protected areas, it is not considered by the [[IUCN]] to be threatened.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />
